title: Preparation of antiserum and detection of proteins by Western blotting using the starlet sea anemone, _Nematostella vectensis_
protocol: Predict the amino acid sequence of your protein of interest from an in-house generated cDNA sequence or EST databases.
Send the cDNA sequence to a commercial source for selection of a suitable epitope.
Choose an epitope of approximately 18 aa at the extreme C terminus.
Use rabbits as the animal model to generate abundant, highly specific antiserum.
Instruct the company to use BSA as the carrier protein.
Purify the antiserum to obtain optimal, clean Western blots.
Store the antiserum at -80°C for long-term storage.
Keep small aliquots of 75-100 μl at -20°C for frequent use.
Generate a cDNA from purified _Nematostella_ RNA.
Subclone the cDNA into a mammalian cell overexpression vector using standard recombinant DNA techniques.
Transfect 50-70% confluent A293 cells with 10 µg of the _Nematostella_ protein expression vector and an empty vector as control.
Two days post-transfection, remove medium from cells.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Lysate the cells in AT buffer to a final volume of 160 µl.
Determine protein concentration in the clarified lysate using an assay such as Bradford.
Store the lysate at -80°C prior to use.
Prepare _Nematostella_ protein extract according to standard procedures.
Transfer 25 µg of _Nematostella_ protein extract to a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 4X SDS sample buffer to achieve a final concentration of 1X.
Heat the sample at 95-100°C for 10 minutes on a heating block.
Load samples onto an SDS-polyacrylamide gel, suitable for proteins between 40 and 100 kDa.
Load approximately 10-20 µg of cell lysates from both empty vector- and pcDNA-gene vector-transfected cells as controls.
Electrophorese samples at 80 V until the bromophenol blue passes through the stacking gel and into the resolving gel.
Increase voltage to 160 V and electrophorese until the bromophenol blue reaches the bottom of the resolving gel.
Disassemble the apparatus, and discard the stacking gel.
Load the resolving gel onto the electro-blotting transfer apparatus.
Transfer the gel to a nitrocellulose membrane at 100 V for 1-2 hours.
Wash the membrane twice with PBS for 1 minute each.
Block membranes with 25 ml Western Blocking Buffer for at least 1 hour at room temperature, or overnight at 4°C.
Probe membranes with primary antiserum diluted in Western Blocking Buffer for the appropriate length of time.
Wash membranes four times with TBST for 10 minutes each.
Probe membranes with secondary antiserum for an appropriate length of time.
Wash membranes 4 times with TBST for 10 minutes each.
Wash membrane 2 times with TBS for 5 minutes each.
Add ECL solution and detect proteins according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Mix luminol and peroxide buffer in equal volumes (0.5 ml each).
Transfer the mixed ECL solution onto the nitrocellulose membrane.
Incubate the membrane with the ECL solution for 5 minutes.
Pour off the ECL solution from the membrane.
Detect luminescence by incubating the membrane with x-ray film.
Exposure of the film to the nitrocellulose membrane can take between 15 seconds and 5 minutes.
